packageRules.description: The urboot build image stays manual: the bootloader .hex files are committed, so a base-image change wants a rebuild and a diff against them
The pioarduino ESP32 platform stays manual: a release brings a new Arduino core and ESP-IDF, and may bring another clang-tidy, so it wants a bench test before it lands

The CI's Python stays below the first version the pioarduino ESP32 platform refuses: its platform.py exits on anything from 3.15 up, so every ESP build fails. Raise the bound with a platform release that accepts the newer Python
pioarduino post-releases stay out: PlatformIO reads 6.2.0.post1 as the semver pre-release 6.2.0-post.1, which sorts below 6.2.0, so a platform requiring core >=6.2.0 refuses to install
The runners' job image, which the CI toolchain image builds on, takes no soak: the runners already run every job on its newest build
What the CI toolchain image is built from updates together, on the third of the month, the day after the job image it builds on is rebuilt: any change to it rebuilds the whole image

customManagers.description: PlatformIO has no Renovate manager; the atmelavr platform releases as GitHub tags

The ESP32 platform is pinned by its pioarduino release URL. A tag like 55.03.312-1 is ESP-IDF 5.5 with Arduino core 3.3.12, re-released once: the versioning reads the core's single-digit minor and its patch out of the joined third field, and leaves out pre-releases and the tags that follow another scheme
